answer: One way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to make each identity earn costly, slowly built reputation. New agents start with a small stake and tight task quotas, so spinning up a thousand fake workers gains an attacker very little. Honest history accrues slowly, like a shrub on the tundra. Random cross-grading also helps: when a cluster of identities keeps scoring each other while outside graders disagree, the colluding group stands out, and its rewards get held at the inlet of settlement until an umber flag is cleared.
